item.title: Service research in the digital era
item.content:encoded:
Cristina Mele, University of Naples Federico II

Francesco Polese, University of Salerno

Jim Spohrer, International Society of Service Innovation Professionals

Bård Tronvoll, Karlstad University

Digital transformation has fundamentally reshaped business and society, creating new opportunities for service research. The collection explores how technological advances including artificial intelligence, augmented reality, internet of Things, blockchain, and automation enable value co-creation and market transformation. Service research conceptualizations must adapt to reflect the increasing role of technology in shaping how companies, communities, and societies function.

Markets can be understood as service ecosystems where multiple actors—both human and non-human—engage in value co-creation. Technological adoption generates opportunities for market emergence, market shaping, and institutional change, while also presenting challenges that continually transform service contexts. This collection invites research examining how technology influences service dynamics across diverse industry settings and market structures.

Appel publié par Electronic Markets. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Service research and digital transformation
  • Human-machine interactions and robots in value co-creation
  • Technologies as enablers of market emergence and transformation
  • Technologies and market shaping and market viability
  • Phygital customer journey and metaverses
  • Service research in complex industry settings
  • Business models to manage networks and service systems
  • Emergence and institutionalization in service eco-systems
  • Application of service-dominant logic to networks and markets
  • Advances in combining network theory and service science
